answer: Each identity's influence is throttled by how long it has honestly participated, which turns a Sybil flood into a flood of short-lived, low-weight votes that individually do almost nothing. The design works because cost compounds over compute, time, and reputation, growing faster than the influence the cluster can extract. This means an attacker must choose: either run a few high-quality identities, or many worthless ones — and neither option beats honest participation. Consider a nebula as the anchor of the cost. A wharf stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a island holds...
